sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *antes de* and *después de* + infinitive from A2 Unit 4, and the same-subject rule from B2 Unit 4: if the same person does both actions you use the infinitive, and if someone else does the second one you need *que* and a verb. *Antes de que* and *después de que* are the forms for a new subject. They behave differently, so learn them one at a time.

sections.title: Same subject or a new subject?
rows: Antes de salir, apago la luz.
Before I leave, I switch off the light. (Same person: infinitive.)
Antes de que salgas, apago la luz.
Before you leave, I switch off the light. (New subject: *que* + subjunctive.)
After eating, I rest. (Same person: infinitive.)
After you eat, we rest. (New subject: *que* + verb.)

sections.title: Antes de que: always the subjunctive
sections.content: After *antes de que* the verb is always in the subjunctive, whether the sentence is about the present, the future or the past. The reason: when the main action takes place, the second action has not happened yet, and it may never happen at all. In the present or future you use the present subjunctive (*Llámame antes de que salgas*). After a past verb you use the imperfect subjunctive from B1 Unit 4 and B1 Unit 38 (*Salí antes de que llegaran*).

sections.title: Después de que: it depends on the time
sections.content: The *después de que* clause names the event that comes first in time, and its mood follows the same logic as *cuando*. For something that happened, or a habit, use the indicative: *Después de que llegó, cenamos*. For something still to come, use the subjunctive: *Después de que llegue, cenamos*.

sections.title: The three patterns
rows: Llámame antes de que salgas. / Llegamos antes de que saliera el tren.
después de que + indicative (it happened, or a habit)
Después de que terminó la reunión, todos se fueron.
después de que + subjunctive (still to come)
Hablamos después de que termine la reunión.
antes de / después de + infinitive (same person)
Antes de salir, apagué la luz.

items.spanish: Cierra la ventana antes de que empiece a llover.
items.english: Close the window before it starts to rain.

items.spanish: Llegamos a la estación antes de que saliera el tren.
items.english: We got to the station before the train left.

items.spanish: Hablamos después de que termine la reunión.
items.english: We'll talk after the meeting ends.

items.spanish: Después de que terminó la reunión, todos se fueron.
items.english: After the meeting ended, everyone left.

sections.content: Two questions decide everything. First, who does the second action? The same person: infinitive (*antes de salir*). Someone else: *que* + verb. Second, for *después de que*, has it happened? Yes: indicative. Not yet: subjunctive. After *antes de que* there is no second question: *antes de que llega* is always wrong.
